A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KDF/KDN methods, simulations and human study despite the changed title. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v4's Appendix A was inspected; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original experiments on five synthetic classification distributions and a human study with 126 retained participants, supported by Figures 1–3 and Table 1.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulation experiments and human-study results in Figures 1–3 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same polytope construction, neighborhood weighting, Gaussian estimation, density bias and Bayesian inference. The Kragen framing and duplicated appendix pseudocode introduce no new procedure. The revised formal OOD target does not change the existing inference rule.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Gaussian XOR, Spiral, Circle, Sinewave and Polynomial simulations, plus human judgments on Gaussian XOR and Spiral. The generative-model framing adds no evaluated dataset, task or test scenario.

E2.justification: The machine comparisons retain RF and the same neural-network parent model against KDF and KDN. NN becomes DN terminology. Likewise, Figure 3's MLP becomes DN while retaining the stated single-hidden-layer model and RF comparison.

E3.justification: The evaluation regions, metrics, sample sizes, 500-tree forests, four-layer networks, optimizer settings and human-study procedures remain unchanged. v4's Table 1 caption incorrectly calls FPR@95 a false-negative rate while the body retains false-positive rate; this inconsistency does not establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The sample-size analyses, posterior visualizations, OOD-confidence analyses and human-versus-model case study are retained. Figure 3's redraw does not introduce a new analysis, and Appendix A contains pseudocode rather than additional experiments.

E5.justification: v4 adds ± quantities throughout Table 1, where v1 gives point values, but does not define whether these are standard deviations, standard errors or intervals. Figure 2 retains medians over 45 repetitions and 25th–75th percentile bands. No increased run count is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 materially revises network results across all five simulations. For Circle and Polynomial, KDN AUROC changes from 0.87 to 0.99 and 0.79 to 0.99; NN/DN FPR@95 changes from 0.98 to 0.87 and 0.990 to 0.79. These revise the principal OOD comparison, although corrections versus recomputation are not explained.

T1.justification: v4 adds Section 4, Theorem 1 and its derivation claiming asymptotic unbiasedness under shrinking polytopes, growing within-polytope counts and vanishing count fractions. Equation 2.1 also changes the desired OOD output from uniform 1/K to the class prior P[Y=k], a substantive mathematical correction.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes OOD detection without compromising in-distribution performance. v4's abstract presents discriminative-to-generative conversion, claims comparative theoretical efficiency and sampling capability, and asserts different advantages at small and large sample sizes. This substantially broadens and qualifies the stated contributions.

C2.justification: The new abstract acknowledges low-dimensional evidence and possible discriminative-model advantages at larger sample sizes. Section 2.1 explicitly distinguishes the paper's disjoint-support OOD setting from overlapping-support OOD learning. Most discussion remains unchanged, including the conclusion's unqualified no-sacrifice claim.

D1.justification: Model settings, optimization details, human-study instructions and the code-access statement are retained. Appendix A repeats existing fitting and KDN pseudocode and contains an empty KDF routine; it supplies no substantive new implementation instructions, while the complete main-text routine remains available.

R1.justification: The same 15 references remain, but the title and abstract reposition the contribution from OOD detection to bridging discriminative and generative modeling, invoking the histogram-rule/kernel-density relationship. Section 2.1 additionally contrasts the OOD definition with the already-cited OOD-learning literature.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, the opening motivation changes, author information is edited, and neural-network terminology becomes deep-network terminology. A Theory section and Appendix A are inserted, but most existing prose and the main exposition sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is rescaled to accommodate uncertainty values, bolded entries and an expanded caption. Figure 3 changes colors, labels and binary-posterior orientation while retaining its substantive comparison. Figures 1–2 largely retain their displays, and the appendix adds duplicate algorithm blocks.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 2.1 to the class-prior limit and adding table variability are useful. However, the new abstract claims comparative theoretical efficiency that Theorem 1's asymptotic-unbiasedness argument does not establish, and its sample-size tradeoffs conflict with the retained no-sacrifice conclusion. Undefined ± quantities and an unfinished duplicate appendix further reduce clarity. These inconsistencies produce a limited decline in coherence and evidential support despite the useful additions.
